analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop.swift. The only changes are in the head text: a new internal actor property `operatorModelFilter: Set<String>?` (head line ~224) and its initialization (~line 946) from `config.config.backend.enabledModels` unioned with `config.models.map(\.id)`; nil when enabled_models is empty. In the supplied excerpts the property is stored but not consumed. The comment says `operatorFilterAllows` uses it, but that function and the callers that act on coordinator-pushed desired models (prefetch/reconcile, load_model) are outside the supplied units. That is a limit on coverage, not evidence that anything is safe or unsafe.

Security-relevant observation: a nil filter (empty enabled_models) means any coordinator-pushed model is served. This matches the pre-existing behavior stated in the comment, so it is not a regression. The coordinator is trusted in this model. The filter only narrows what the provider will serve, which is an additive restriction and does not touch the A-001, A-003 or A-004 flows, attestation, App Attest authorization (A-016, TB-011), the cache (T-041) or the add-on hold (TB-012) paths.

The base unit (lines 1024-1290) is unchanged context. It covers ModelSlot, attestation signer selection and the companion-file list. I saw no change there.

For integration: check the consumers of `operatorModelFilter` in the Prefetch, Preload and model-switch extensions. Confirm that live operator switches update it consistently, that the union with the startup models is intended, and that the filter cannot be bypassed by autopilot or desired-model paths. Those files were not supplied.
